_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401883110.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night (20:30 Spanish time): Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games (10 scored, 32 conceded) and have lost five in a row, while Almería have 32 points, 26 scored and 11 conceded, and are twelve games unbeaten in league and cup; Castellón's weekend win means they need to win here to go back top. Sergio Lobera, in his first full week and first home game in charge after a 2-0 loss at Tenerife, calls it a chance for a turning point, wants the Murube full (season-ticket holders get free tickets) and mentioned absences without naming anyone. Almería's squad list confirms captain Jorge Pulido is a late absence with an ankle problem, alongside Rodrigo Ely and Nico Melamed; only Melamed is in the numbers (about -6% on their goals), while Marcos Luna, Stefan Dzodic (back from a ban) and Brian Cipenga (back from international duty) return. Referee Eder Mallo Fernández, confirmed with Rubén Ávalos on VAR, gives about 5.5 cards a game, near the league average, and that record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already taking about 6% off Almería for Melamed and adding a little to Ceuta from last season's 3-2 home win in this fixture. What they don't see is now confirmed: Almería lose centre-back and captain Pulido late (Ely is also out), which should help Ceuta's thin attack led by Jordi Escobar, while Almería get Dzodic and Cipenga back and must win to retake top spot. Both sides point slightly up, so a mild +3%, about 3.3 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, already including their recent run of 44 corners in six games (+11% momentum). García Pimienta expects Ceuta to want the ball at home, which fits Lobera's possession style with high full-backs, and Almería with Cipenga back have more width on the break; none of this changes the corner count beyond what the numbers already see, so 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum) and referee Eder Mallo Fernández, whose 5.5 cards a game is close to the league average (+2.5%). A desperate home side in front of a full ground may foul to stop Almería's counters, but that is the pattern the numbers already see and there is no derby or other edge here, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.5 shots, with Ceuta's recent volume adding about 31% to their side and Almería's quieter attacking run taking about 7% off theirs. Lobera wants balance rather than all-out attack, and Almería without Pulido may concede a few more efforts but need few chances themselves; that sits within what the numbers already give, so 31.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. Ceuta hit the target only twice at Tenerife despite most of the ball and Lobera admits they score too little, which argues lower, but a reshuffled Almería back line without Pulido and Ely should make clean shots a little easier for them; those offset, so I stay at 10.3.

401875009.overall: Two struggling sides meet on Monday night: Monza are 18th with 7 points after four straight defeats, and Paolo Vanoli's Fiorentina are 15th with 9 points, unbeaten in three and scoring in ten straight games. Ivan Juric is banned and watches from the stands, so assistant Matteo Paro leads Monza; Juric asked for 'rage' against Fiorentina, and local press frame the game as one that could decide his future. Captain Pessina is back in the squad after three months out but will probably start on the bench, while Folorunsho (counted), Maye and Ngonge are out; Varela (9 goals in 10 games) leads the line. Fiorentina have Atta back in the squad for gradual minutes, Ndour recovered and Njie a late doubt with a thigh problem (Gnonto ready to start), with Pongracic and Parisi (both counted) out. Referee Daniele Doveri is one of Serie A's most lenient (2.7 cards a game), which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already adding a little for both sides' recent scoring and leaky defending and taking about 4% off Fiorentina for Pongracic. Monza miss Ngonge and Maye, who are not in the numbers' list, but they have been out for weeks so recent form already reflects it, and top scorer Varela starts; Fiorentina have scored in ten straight games and get Atta and Ndour back. Nothing moves the total, so about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, already nudging up for Fiorentina's recent corner count (32 in six). Monza's 3-4-2-1 with Birindelli and Mangas as wing-backs and Fiorentina's 4-2-3-1 with Mastantuono and Njie or Gnonto wide are both sides' usual shapes, so I stay at about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already cut by about 29% for Doveri's lenient record, which I don't size again. This is a relegation scrap between sides two points apart, with Juric banned, his job reportedly on the line and him publicly asking his players for 'rage'; that tends to bring more fouls than a usual Doveri match, so a mild lean up to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already raised for both sides' recent shooting (+9% Monza, +14% Fiorentina). Monza need to attack at home and Fiorentina are close to full strength, but that is the picture the numbers already have, so about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already lifted around 10% for each side's recent accuracy. Varela leads Monza's line with Mota and Robinson behind him, and Pellegrino leads Fiorentina's with Mastantuono and Gonçalves; nothing in the team news changes that, so about 10.

401879237.overall: Brentford (10th, 14 points, beaten 2-0 at Brighton before the break) host Everton (7th, 16 points, three straight wins in all competitions including 1-0 at Newcastle and a home win over Coventry) on Monday night, two points apart. Brentford are badly hit: Igor Thiago serves a ban after his red card at Brighton (the numbers count it, about -12.5% on their goals), Nathan Collins (knee) and Aaron Hickey (hamstring) are out for weeks, Rico Henry and Kaye Furo are sidelined, Dasilva and Milambo were only due a B-team run-out on Sunday, and Fabio Carvalho may make the squad; Callum Wilson is expected to lead the line. Everton report no new injuries, Moyes saying no one is ruled out, and are expected in their usual 4-2-3-1 with Thierno Barry (six league goals, the league's top xG) up front; Moyes becomes Everton's outright record holder for games managed tonight. Match-day checks found no change from this morning, and referee Craig Pawson (26 yellows and one red in six league games; 3.7 cards a game on record) is already counted, so the view stays as it was.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already taking about 12.5% off Brentford for Thiago's ban. They count missing players only by goals and assists, so they barely feel the loss of first-choice defenders Collins and Hickey, which helps Barry, the league's top chance-getter and strong in the air against a Brentford back line that relies on aerial duels. Wilson starting and Carvalho's possible return soften Brentford's attacking loss, so I keep it mild: about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, already counting Brentford's low recent corner count (21 in six) and Everton's slightly higher one. Brentford still play wide and cross a lot, with a stand-in on the left for Hickey, and Everton line up in their usual 4-2-3-1, so nothing on match day points away from 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowered about 10% for referee Craig Pawson's record and for calm past meetings. Everton have no suspensions and Moyes reports a fit squad, the table gap is two points and there is no rivalry between these clubs, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already raising Everton for their recent volume (81 shots in six). Brentford lose Thiago's shooting but Wilson starts, while a weakened Brentford defence should let Everton's midfield trio of Armstrong, Garner and Dewsbury-Hall push on; the two roughly balance, so 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Brentford for poor recent accuracy (19 on target in six). Losing Thiago's finishing is offset by Barry facing a back four without Collins and Hickey, so I stay at 8.2.

401882802.overall: A Monday-night Valencian relegation derby: Levante (18th, 11 points) host Elche (19th, 10 points), so the winner climbs past the other and possibly out of the drop zone. Luís Castro has the whole Levante squad available, with Manu Sánchez back from a hamstring injury and only Nakoha listed as a doubt. Martín Anselmi's Elche miss playmaker Marc Aguado (ankle), Adam Boayar and Yago, none of whom the numbers list (they only take off Ali Houary), while Villar, Sangaré and Lemar are back in training, Revivo was a midweek doubt and Cepeda returned late from Chile; Elche have lost their last two without scoring. Referee Francisco José Hernández Maeso (4.2 cards a game) is already counted, but the numbers do not flag the derby or the relegation stakes; no confirmed lineups yet at this refresh, so the view from this morning holds with the card lean trimmed slightly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, high for two bottom-three sides, and their momentum trims Elche only slightly even though they have failed to score in their last two. Elche are without Marc Aguado, who runs their midfield and is not in the numbers, and a six-pointer between sides a point apart tends to be cautious; a mild lean down to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's, and already count Elche's recent 31 corners in six games. Levante should take the initiative at home with Manu Sánchez back on the left, while Elche keep the ball and cross; nothing in the team news shifts that, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already including referee Hernández Maeso (about -12% for his 4.2 a game) and Levante's light recent booking count, which I don't size again. What they don't flag is that this is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between sides a point apart, which usually brings more fouls and bookings; a moderate lean up to about 4.1, a touch below this morning's view because cards takes have run hot lately.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.5 shots and already add for both sides' recent shooting, with Levante conceding 103 in their last six. Levante with Iván Romero and Etta Eyong should press at home, but a nervy six-pointer could slow the game; nothing points clearly either way, so 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Levante have a full squad, and Elche's recent blanks are more about finishing than about getting shots on target, which the numbers' momentum already reflects; without Aguado their supply may dip a little, but not enough to move, so 8.9.

401915380.overall: Bodø/Glimt are 25th of 36 with 4 points, both earned at home (1-0 against Dortmund, 0-0 against Lille), so this game on the Aspmyra artificial pitch is close to a must-win for the play-off places; they lead the Norwegian league and have won 14 of their last 15 league games. LASK are 16th with 6 points and arrive on five straight league wins, but vice-captain Andrés Andrade (ankle) is out, and the numbers now count him (+6.2% on Bodø's goals). Florian Flecker (calf), one of LASK's joint top Champions League scorers, is also out and is still not counted; Bello and Harakaté are out and counted, as are Evjen (knee) and Mikkelsen (groin) for Bodø. Line-ups are due an hour before kick-off and the match-day previews still show the same expected XIs as this morning, with Usor up front for LASK and Hauge and Blomberg wide for Bodø. Turkish referee Halil Umut Meler, whose higher card rate is already counted, is in charge on a cold night under floodlights.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals (2.9 Bodø, 1.1 LASK); since this morning they also count Andrade's absence (+6.2% for Bodø), plus LASK's hot scoring run (+2.8%) and Evjen, Mikkelsen and Bello. What they still cannot see is Flecker, one of LASK's main Champions League scorers, missing from every predicted XI, and Bodø's two home games in this competition produced one goal in total. I keep -4%, about 3.8 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, 5.9 of them for Bodø as the side expected to have the ball, with both teams' recent corner counts (+0.8% and -1.0%) already in. LASK's 3-5-2 with wing-backs Jørgensen and Dibango and Bodø's wide attack through Blomberg and Hauge are both confirmed in today's predicted line-ups, which is what the numbers expect, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already adding referee Halil Umut Meler's 4.5 cards a game (+7.5%) and taking off LASK's low recent card count (-6.6%) and Bodø's (-2.1%). There is no rivalry; a reshuffled LASK back three without Andrade on a fast artificial pitch, which Kühbauer calls an extra challenge, may be stretched a little, but that is a normal away-team picture, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots (14.4 Bodø, 12.5 LASK), already trimmed for Bodø's quieter recent shooting (-3.9%). Bodø need the win and will push, while Kühbauer says LASK want to take something home and will still play two strikers without Flecker; these pull both ways, so I stay at 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already counting LASK's sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and Bodø's slight dip (-2.0%). The LASK absences (Andrade at the back, Flecker up front) roughly cancel for shots on target, and I have put the net effect into goals rather than counting it twice, so I stay at 10.5.

401915300.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9; Galatasaray have won their last two Champions League games (Lille, Stuttgart) and want a top-24 place, while Villa lost 3-0 at Barcelona last time and Emery admits a top-8 finish is out of their hands. Osimhen, Leão and Sallai are out and the numbers count all three on goals; Sporx's match-day page still lists Osimhen as injured, with Jakobs a doubt, and the predicted XIs have no recognised centre-forward: Barış Alper Yılmaz, Yunus Akgün and Batrakov in attack with Lemina beside Torreira. Villa are without Cash, Ruggeri and Onana (all counted); Lindelöf was a doubt with illness, so Harwood-Bellis is expected alongside Pau Torres. Line-ups come an hour before kick-off and nothing has changed since this morning. German referee Daniel Siebert, average on cards and already counted, is in charge on a repaired RAMS Park pitch.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (1.1 Galatasaray, 1.8 Villa) and already take off Osimhen (-10%), Sallai and Leão (-5% each) from Galatasaray's goals, plus Cash for Villa. The striker-less plan is just the other side of Osimhen's absence; one report says he might sit on the bench, but at most for a late cameo, so nothing new moves the total and I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's slight rise in corners won (+2.9%) and Villa's dip (-3.4%). Villa keep the ball and push wide with Maatsen and Wan-Bissaka, while Galatasaray lose width without Leão and Sallai and, in today's Turkish line-ups, play Lemina in a more solid midfield; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-8.4%), Villa's slight rise (+3.7%) and Daniel Siebert's average record (4.1 a game, +1%) already in. RAMS Park is loud and both sides need points, and a patched pitch can bring a few clumsy challenges, but that is close to a normal Champions League night here, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots (12.8 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa); they take the missing forwards off goals but not off shots. With Osimhen, Sallai and Leão all out, no centre-forward in the predicted XI and Lemina added as a second holding midfielder, Galatasaray lose their main shot-takers, and a repaired pitch may slow the game; I keep the trim, to about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+5.9%) and Galatasaray's slight dip (-0.8%), but not the forwards Galatasaray are missing. Osimhen is the player who turns their chances into efforts on target and he will not start, so I keep my lean lower, to about 9.7.

401915295.overall: Arsenal are 3rd in the league phase on 10 points and top of the Premier League despite Saturday's 2-2 draw at Newcastle; Dortmund are 12th on 9 points and top of the Bundesliga. Match-day previews confirm David Raya is out with the shoulder he hurt at Newcastle (no surgery needed), so Kepa starts in goal, and Zubimendi (hamstring) and Saka (quad) are also out; the numbers count Saka (about -10% on Arsenal's goals) and Raya, but not Zubimendi. Sports Mole expects Gyokeres, White, Hincapie and Lewis-Skelly back in the XI, with Saliba still not fit to start. For Dortmund, Emre Can, Inacio, Konstantelias, Lerma and Kaba are out; Guirassy is in the squad but UEFA still lists him doubtful with a thigh problem, so Fabio Silva or Beier is expected to lead the line. Italian referee Maurizio Mariani, slightly below average on cards, is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals; they already take about 10% off Arsenal for Saka and add a little to Dortmund for Raya's absence. Arsenal also miss Zubimendi's control in midfield, which the numbers don't count, and Dortmund have Guirassy available at least from the bench, so I stay a touch higher: 2.5 x 1.02, about 2.55.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Arsenal around 6.3 and Dortmund's busier recent corner count already in (+3.0%). Arsenal build corners from sustained pressure and set pieces even without Saka, with Madueke and Eze expected wide, and Dortmund tend to defend deep away in a back three; both records already show this, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards, already adding about 13% to Arsenal for their high recent card count and trimming a little for Maurizio Mariani, who averages 3.9 cards a game against a 4.1 average. There are no bans and no needle between the clubs, so nothing new points either way; I stay at 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Dortmund's busy recent shooting already counted (+11.3%) and Arsenal's (+5.7%). Gyokeres is expected back up front for Arsenal, but they still miss Saka's output on the right and Zubimendi's control, while Guirassy is at best a substitute for Dortmund. These roughly cancel, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target, including a small boost for Dortmund's recent accuracy (+2.7%). Guirassy, Dortmund's most clinical finisher, is still listed doubtful and likely starts on the bench, and Arsenal have been less incisive without Saka, so nothing clearly moves it; I stay at 8.6.

401915296.overall: Como are 4th on 9 points in their first Champions League season and beat Cagliari 2-0 on Saturday; AEK are 29th on 3 points and need a result. Kean, Diao, Addai and Jesus Rodriguez are out for Como, but today's previews (UEFA, The Stats Zone) list Caqueret only as a doubt rather than out, Chalobah is fit again and Fabregas is expected to field Da Cunha, Nico Paz and Baturina behind Douvikas, so Como's attack looks stronger than it did this morning. The numbers take a little off for Diao and Kean and ride Como's 17 goals in six games. AEK travel without the suspended Koita and Zubkov (Arriaga is listed out by UEFA, though one preview still has him in the XI), and Fabregas calls them physical and dominant. Spanish referee Javier Alberola Rojas, who has averaged about 4.7 yellows a game this season, is in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already trimming Como for Diao and Kean while adding 4.3% for their recent scoring. Caqueret is now only doubtful and Nico Paz, Baturina and Da Cunha are expected to start, so I soften this morning's -5; what is left is Como without natural wingers and AEK without Koita, a UEFA ban the numbers don't know about: 2.9 x 0.97, about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, with Como around 5.6 and both sides' small recent dips already in. Without natural wingers Como's width comes from full-backs Valle and Couto, who already supplied much of it, and AEK are likely to defend deep away from home; nothing clearly moves the count, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already take about 16% off Como for how few cards they have picked up lately, plus 7% off AEK. Alberola Rojas has shown about 4.7 yellows a game this season, a little busier than average, and Fabregas calls AEK physical, but the referee's record and AEK's style are already in the numbers, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.4 shots, with small recent dips counted on both sides. Como are still short of forwards (Kean, Diao, Addai and Rodriguez out) and AEK lose Koita, one of their most frequent shooters, whom the numbers still count; with Paz and Baturina expected to start I keep the trim small: 25.4 x 0.98, about 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, with Como's sharp recent finishing counted. Koita's ban removes much of AEK's threat from wide, which the numbers don't see, and Como rely on Douvikas alone up front, though their creative midfielders are fit, so I go slightly lower: 9.3 x 0.97, about 9.0.

401915294.overall: Both sides have 3 points: Feyenoord are 32nd and Porto 26th, and both need wins to stay in the race for the top 24. Feyenoord are six games without a win after Saturday's 3-2 home defeat to Excelsior and have conceded eight in their last two league games, leaving Giovanni van Bronckhorst under pressure; Hadj Moussa is in the predicted XI after an ankle knock, but centre-back Watanabe is a doubt with a foot problem (not in the numbers), and St. Juste, Bos, Nieuwkoop, Beelen and Moder are out, St. Juste already counted. Porto lead the Portuguese league by five points, unbeaten in 11, and beat Napoli 4-1 last time out in Europe; Smalling is not in their Champions League squad and William Gomes is back in training but uncertain. Farioli expects a physical game with many duels and wants to press high. Bosnian referee Irfan Peljto, who gives fewer cards than average over his career, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already add a little to Porto for St. Juste's absence. Two sides who both need a win, a Feyenoord defence that has leaked eight in two league games and may also lose Watanabe, and a Porto side planning to press high point to an open game: 2.9 x 1.03, about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, with Feyenoord's lower recent count already in (-4.0%). Feyenoord usually have most of the ball at home and Hadj Moussa's dribbling helps them win corners, while Porto's full-backs push high; that is in both normal records, so I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and count Irfan Peljto's low card rate (-9.2%) and both sides' calm recent discipline. Farioli expects a physical game full of duels, which could add a booking, but Peljto lets a lot go over his career, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already add about 13% to Porto for how many shots Feyenoord have been conceding. Both teams must chase a win and Porto want to win the ball high, which tends to create quick shots on both sides: 26.3 x 1.02, about 26.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, including a 12.6% boost for Porto from Feyenoord's poor recent defending and a 4.7% cut for Feyenoord's poor finishing. With Hadj Moussa expected to start and Porto in form in front of goal, in a game both need to win, I go slightly up: 9.6 x 1.02, about 9.8.

401915379.overall: Manchester City are 7th on 9 points but come in on four Premier League games without a win after Saturday's 1-1 home draw with Fulham, with Arsenal away on Sunday; Maresca wants a top-eight finish. Only Semenyo is out (already counted) and Matheus Nunes is fit again; today's previews expect only limited rotation, with Haaland, Doku and Cherki starting and Khusanov at right-back. Allegri's Napoli, 27th on 3 points, are without Buongiorno (meniscus), Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Meret, Badiashile, Vergara and Alisson Santos, and Rafa Marin is suspended, leaving Rrahmani and Beukema as the only fit specialist centre-backs; reports differ on whether Neres is fit. The numbers count Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Vergara and Rafa Marin but not Buongiorno. Romanian referee Istvan Kovacs, an average carder, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already take off for Semenyo, Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Vergara and the suspended Rafa Marin. They do not know Buongiorno is also out, leaving Napoli with two fit specialist centre-backs against Haaland, and today's previews expect City to rotate less than feared this morning, so I go a little further: 3.4 x 1.05, about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, mostly City's, and already add about 10% for how many corners Napoli have conceded lately. With a patched-up defence Napoli should be pinned back even more than their record shows, and blocked crosses from Doku and Ndiaye turn into corners: a mild lean up, to about 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Napoli's busier recent card count (+12%) and Istvan Kovacs's average record included, so I do not lean on the referee. What is left is a stand-in Napoli back line, likely with Politano at right-back, chasing City's wingers and likely to give away fouls: a small lean up, to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots and already add about 13% to City for the volume Napoli have been allowing. Buongiorno's absence is not in that figure, and with Haaland, Doku and Cherki expected to start City should have even more of the ball, so I go up a bit more than this morning: 28.6 x 1.04, about 29.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, with Napoli's sharp recent finishing (+8%) already counted. A weakened Napoli back line should let City shoot from closer in, and City's attack is expected near full strength, though they managed little against Fulham, so I keep the move small: 10.4 x 1.04, about 10.8.

401915299.overall: RB Leipzig (30th) and Lens (33rd) both have 3 points from four games and need a win to stay in the race for the top 24; Leipzig are 4th in the Bundesliga under Martin Demichelis after a 5-1 win at Union Berlin, Lens drew 1-1 with Toulouse in Didier Digard's first game after the 9-1 loss at Como. Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba (bruised knee) missed the final training session and is out, and he is not on the numbers' missing list, so Orban and Esteve are expected to pair at the back; Ouedraogo and Guiu are still out (counted). Three French outlets expect a back three with Ganiou and Abdulhamid wide, Haidara and Titraoui in midfield and Thauvin, Hazard and Sima in attack. Slovak referee Ivan Kruzliak, a little below average on cards, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, already adding about 8% to Leipzig for their recent scoring and taking a little off Lens for Cuisance and Edouard. Lukeba's absence is confirmed today but is not in the numbers, so a reshuffled Leipzig back line faces a Lens front three of Thauvin, Hazard and the returning Sima. A small nudge up: 3.5 x 1.03, about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, split fairly evenly, with small recent dips counted on both sides. Lens are expected in a back three with a centre-back, Ganiou, at left wing-back and Aguilar out on the right, so they look less of a crossing side, while Leipzig still go wide through Nusa and Raum. That balances out, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Leipzig's quieter recent record (-8%) and Ivan Kruzliak's slightly low card rate (-5.4%) counted. Both sides need the win and Demichelis expects a strong reaction from Lens after the Como defeat, but there is no history of bad blood and no ban in play, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots, adding about 7% to Leipzig for their busy recent shooting and trimming Lens (-9%) for their low count. Lens lose Cuisance and Edouard but get Sima back up front, and Leipzig miss Lukeba at the back rather than any attacker, so the volume of shooting should look like the numbers expect. I stay at 28.5.

401915291.overall: Atletico Madrid (26th, 4 points) and Viking (25th, 4 points) sit one place apart in the clubs' first meeting, and Atletico, after losing to Liverpool and Bayern, need to win at home to keep any hope of the top eight. cards.text: The numbers say 2.9 cards, already taking about 16% off for Lambrechts' low card rate and both sides' calm recent runs. There is no rivalry, Viking play an open, passing game and nothing in the news points to a nastier match, so I stay at 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.9 shots (21.0 Atletico, 9.9 Viking), already lifted for Viking's busy recent shooting. Viking's illness could cut their shots a little while Atletico should dominate even more, which roughly cancels out, so I stay at 30.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, with Letexier's average record barely moving them and Inter's calm recent run counted. There is no rivalry and nothing in the news points to a rougher game, so I stay at 3.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, 5.3 for Shakhtar, already lifted for their recent corner run and cut for Fenerbahce's. A near-neutral venue and an open game with both sides needing points fit that figure, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, the highest of tonight's games, with Michael Oliver's close-to-average record barely moving them. Turan has asked for aggression and energy and both sides need the points, but that busy-game picture is already in both teams' card records, so I stay at 4.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, fairly even (4.3 Sporting, 5.0 United). Sporting's low-block spells could give United more corners and Sporting fewer, which roughly cancels out, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already taking about 9% off for Marciniak's record and 11% for Sporting's calm recent run, and adding a little for United's busier one. shots.text: The numbers say 29.0 shots, lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Without Cunha United lose a player who shoots a lot from outside the box, and Sporting will defend deeper at times and look to counter, so I trim to about 28.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning only 12 in their last six and lifting Mjällby a little for 17 in their last three. shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. 401915815.overall: Ajax (11th of 36, 6 points) host FC Thun (19th, 3 points) three days before Sunday's Klassieker at Feyenoord. Ajax have won six of their last seven, but earlier this week lost midfielder Jorthy Mokio to a broken fibula, which the numbers' empty missing list does not know; Dolberg, Adingra and Tsygankov are long-term absences already in Ajax's form, and the latest team-news page lists Brandt and Gaaei as doubts, in line with an earlier Dutch preview that expected Brandt to be rested for Feyenoord. Thun lost 3-2 at Young Boys, rotate a lot (about 62% of the eleven kept over six games) and also have a league game on Sunday; earlier reports had striker Furkan Dursun and midfielder Mattias Käit unlikely to make it. Danish referee Mikkel Redder has now been appointed; the numbers had no referee, and his record (about 3.9 cards a game over his career, fewer this season) is a little below the usual level. News today was thin beyond the referee, so the rest of the view holds.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals, with Ajax expected to score 3.2 on their strong recent form. They don't know Mokio is out, Brandt is listed as a doubt and likely rested before the Klassieker, and Thun's main striker Dursun looks set to miss out, so both attacks are a bit weaker than the numbers assume; I go to about 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, most of them (6.5) for Ajax, who will have most of the ball at home against a Thun side that sits back away from home. A changed Ajax front line still plays the same wide game, so nothing here moves the corner count; I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, with Thun expected to collect more (2.7) as the side chasing the ball, but they had no referee to go on. Danish referee Mikkel Redder has since been named; he averages about 3.9 cards a game over his career and fewer this season, slightly under the usual level, and there is no history between the clubs, so I trim to about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.5 shots, about 20 of them for Ajax. With Brandt doubtful and likely rested, Mokio out and Gloukh possibly saved for Feyenoord, plus Thun missing striker Dursun, I trim slightly to about 29.6; it is a mild lean because Ajax should still have most of the ball.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Ajax's likely rotation of their most creative players before the Klassieker and Thun's loss of their main striker both cut the quality of chances a little, which the numbers can't see, so I go to about 9.2.

401915814.overall: Brighton (5th of 36, 7 points) host Universitatea Craiova (8th, also 7 points), so a top-eight place is at stake for both. Brighton lost 2-0 at Hull on Sunday and play Newcastle at the weekend, and the latest team-news page expects rotation (only 56% of the eleven kept over six games): Struijk is listed as rested and Azeez out with an abdominal strain, while Minteh, Hadjam, Beadle and Chema Andrés are doubts, none of which the numbers list; Mitoma, Ferguson, Tzimas and Yohanna are out and counted. Craiova, top in Romania, have named the same eleven in their last two games and report no new absences; keeper Isenko's absence is counted, and an earlier report of a muscle problem for forward Monday Etim could not be confirmed today. German referee Matthias Jöllenbeck (5.3 cards a game in three on record) is already counted. I keep a small cut on Brighton's attack for rotation and the extra doubts.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, 2.8 of them for Brighton, and already take Mitoma, Ferguson and Tzimas into account. A rotated Brighton side with Newcastle next, Minteh doubtful and Azeez out, against a settled, compact Craiova side, points slightly lower, so I go to about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, 8.3 of them for Brighton, who should have long spells of possession against a Craiova side that defends deep with wing-backs dropping into a back five. That pattern drives corners whichever Brighton players start, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and already add about 6% for referee Matthias Jöllenbeck, who has shown 5.3 cards a game in his three on record. Craiova will spend long periods defending and pick up the larger share (2.6), which the numbers expect; with no rivalry and no new news on the officials, I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, about 22 for Brighton. Several changes are expected before Newcastle, with Struijk rested, Azeez out and Minteh a doubt, which the numbers can't see, so I trim to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. A rotated Brighton attack with fewer of its usual creators points a touch lower, so I go to about 10.1; it stays a small lean because Brighton should still create plenty at home.

401915810.overall: Egnatia (26th of 36, 2 points) host Lincoln Red Imps (22nd, 3 points) at the Air Albania Stadium in Tirana, still looking for a first win at this stage after two draws and a loss; the club sold cheap tickets to fill the ground and says it wants three points. Egnatia lead the Albanian league but lost 1-0 at Skënderbeu at the weekend; defender Bitri is suspended and Bakayoko has a cruciate injury, both in the numbers, while Beqja, Hoxha, Duka, Bakalli and Çullhaj have been out of the European squad since the start of the league phase, so they are already in Egnatia's form. Egnatia rotate heavily (about 40% of the eleven kept over six games) with a league game on Sunday, and Lincoln report no absences. Swedish referee Oscar Johnson has no card record in the numbers. News was thin, and nothing in it is big enough to move the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already add a little for Lincoln because Egnatia's regular defender Bitri is banned. Egnatia should attack at home in front of a bigger crowd, but their heavy rotation is already part of their recent form and Lincoln have a full squad, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.9 for Egnatia as the side expected to push, and they already count Lincoln's recent habit of conceding lots of corners and winning few. Nothing I found on lineups or tactics changes that picture, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, split evenly. Referee Oscar Johnson has no card record in the numbers and I found nothing on his style; with no rivalry between the clubs I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, two thirds of them for Egnatia, and already add about 10% for Egnatia because Lincoln have allowed many shots lately. Possible rotation for Egnatia with a league game on Sunday is the only open question and it is normal for them, so I stay at 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Lincoln report a full squad and Egnatia's absences (Bitri, Bakayoko and the players left out of the European squad) are already counted or already in their form, so I stay at 9.4.

401915811.overall: Hearts (32nd of 36, 1 point) host Monaco (4th, 9 points from 9) at a sold-out Tynecastle; Hearts have not won in nine European games this season and need points, while Monaco are almost through. Hearts arrive after an 8-0 win at Dundee and are a settled side (about 84% of the eleven kept), but nine players including McEntee, Fagan-Walcott, Kingsley, Halkett and Spittal are out, all in the numbers (including a big cut for McEntee). Filipe Luís's Monaco miss Golovin, Ansu Fati and Idumbo (counted) plus young defender Elebi, who is not in the numbers but is not a regular starter; they rotate a fair amount with a Ligue 1 game on Sunday, and Brunner and Balogun are expected to lead the attack. Austrian referee Daniel Schlager, around average at 4.1 cards a game, is already counted. Fresh news today was thin, and nothing new is big enough to move the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.3 for Monaco, and already take big cuts for Hearts without McEntee and for Monaco without Golovin and Idumbo. Monaco's expected front two of Brunner and Balogun is close to full strength, and Hearts' big win at Dundee came against weak opposition, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, nearly even, as Hearts tend to go direct and win set pieces at home while Monaco keep the ball. Nothing in the team news changes that, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count referee Daniel Schlager, close to the average at 4.1 a game over 37 games. A loud Tynecastle and a Hearts side chasing the game could add a booking, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Hearts are expected to keep a similar eleven, and Monaco's usual rotation is already part of their form, with Brunner and Balogun still expected up front, so I see no reason to move from 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, 5.1 for Monaco. The absences that matter on both sides are already counted and Monaco's extra one, Elebi, is a fringe defender, so I stay at 8.8.

401915813.overall: Iberia 1999 (29th of 36, 1 point) host Getafe (31st, 1 point) in Tbilisi; Iberia are unbeaten in three league games and lean on striker Amiran Dzagania, while Getafe probably need wins here and at home to Inter Escaldes to reach the top 24. Getafe have lost three in a row without scoring, including 3-0 to Atlético on Sunday, sit just above the LaLiga drop zone and go to Espanyol on Monday; Bordalás has put the league first, and previews expect rotation. The 21 players at Tuesday's last training before travelling include Mayoral, Satriano, Ünal, Azón and Djené (banned for Monday's league game, free here), but not Carvajal, Boselli or Andrés García (unclear knocks), nor Uche and Juanmi; all but García are in the numbers. Romanian referee Horațiu Feșnic is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 for Getafe. Getafe have not scored in three games, Bordalás has openly put the league first with a must-win trip to Espanyol on Monday, and wing-back Andrés García is missing too, none of which the numbers see; I go to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, 5.1 for Getafe. A rotated Getafe side still plays direct with crosses into the box, so the count should hold; I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already high because Getafe foul a lot, Iberia have picked up many cards lately and referee Horațiu Feșnic has shown 5.5 a game in his two on record. Djené, sent off against Atlético, travels and is likely to play, but that is Getafe's normal profile, so I stay at 5.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots, nearly 16 for Getafe. A rotated Getafe side with league priorities and a blunt attack lately should be cautious, so I trim to about 23.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. With Getafe likely to rest some starters before Espanyol and without a goal in three games, and Juanmi and Uche out (already counted), I go a little lower, to about 7.7.

401915812.overall: Lugano top the Conference League table with 9 points from 3 games (11 scored, 4 conceded) and lead the Swiss league by six points, while Jablonec are 23rd on 2 points with no win in Europe after 2-3 at Freiburg, 0-0 with Brighton and 1-1 at Riga, and lost 1-3 at home to Brno on Saturday. Lugano's club site, RSI, Bluewin and La Regione all confirm Albian Ajeti's ban was cut to two domestic games, so he can play on Thursday (he misses Sunday's league game at Lucerne instead), while the numbers still take him out as suspended, about -16% on Lugano's goals. Croci-Torti said on Wednesday he has no problem rotating with five away games in about 15 days, and Hannes Delcroix is out long term (counted). Jablonec are without keeper Jan Hanus and Kevin-Prince Milla (both counted), with Klemen Mihelak in goal; they have not conceded at home in four European games this season. Referee David Smajc (6.0 cards a game in a small sample) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals but take about 16% off Lugano's scoring for Ajeti as suspended. Lugano's own site confirms his ban is domestic only and he is free for Thursday, and since he misses Sunday at Lucerne he is a natural pick for this game, so I add most of that back, to about 3.3; not all of it, as Croci-Torti may still rotate and Jablonec have kept four clean sheets at home in Europe.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Jablonec, who need a first European win and attack with crosses at home. Ajeti's return changes Lugano's finishing rather than how much of the ball they have, and a few rotated Lugano players should not change their wide play, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already adding about 6% for referee David Smajc (6.0 a game in two on record) and for both sides' recent card counts. Ajeti's red at St. Gallen was a domestic matter and these clubs have never met, so nothing points to an unusually heated game and I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, a fairly open game, already lifted a little for Jablonec's recent volume. Ajeti's return helps Lugano's finishing more than their volume of shots, and the rotation Croci-Torti hinted at pulls slightly the other way, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Jablonec's stand-in keeper Mihelak (Hanus counted) and Ajeti's availability matter more for how many go in than for how many are on target, so I stay at 9.2.

401915739.overall: A Baltic meeting in Kaunas between Kauno Zalgiris, last of 36 with 0 points and a 1-11 goal record (0-4 at Brighton, 1-4 at home to Brann, 0-3 at Lugano), and Riga FC, 20th after three 1-1 draws. Riga parted with coach Adrian Gula on Sunday and named Frenchman Didier Zanetti, twice a Latvian Cup winner with Auda, who has had only a few days to work, so Lithuanian press expect Riga to play their usual attacking style. Both domestic seasons are over (Zalgiris champions, Riga second), and Zalgiris defender Marko Konataras admitted the players are physically and mentally tired at the end of a long season, though coach Zeljko Sopicius said his five internationals returned unhurt and nobody new is injured. Riga's long-term absentee Varslavans is already counted and referee Daniyar Sakhi (3.0 cards in one game) is in the numbers; lineup news was thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already trim Zalgiris for scoring 3 in their last six. Riga play their first game under Zanetti after three straight 1-1 draws, and a tired Zalgiris side at the end of their season has scored once in three European games, so I trim a little to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, 4.9 for Zalgiris at home, already trimmed for their few recent corners. Reports expect Riga to keep their attacking style under the new coach rather than change shape, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already cutting Riga for only 2 cards in their last three and taking a little off for referee Daniyar Sakhi's low record. It is a Baltic meeting but not a real rivalry, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, already lifting Riga (47 shots in their last three) and trimming Zalgiris. Zalgiris' fatigue and the long break could slow the game, but they need a first point at home and Sopicius expects to be the stronger side, so I stay at 27.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target and already cut Zalgiris for only 4 on target in their last three. With no new injuries on either side and only Varslavans out (counted), I stay at 8.5.

401915809.overall: Two sides near the bottom on 1 point each: Pafos are 31st and Midtjylland 34th, so both need a win to stay in the play-off race, and Sa Pinto called the three points essential. Midtjylland lead the Danish league and play the title clash at Copenhagen on Sunday; Mike Tullberg said after the Brondby win that the Conference League has been deprioritised because of their injury list, and keeper Bakker, Diao, Castillo, Watjen and others are on the numbers' list. Pafos lose Lele to a ban for his red card at Twente, which the numbers no longer take off (their estimate has risen to 2.9 goals), and injured winger Ngamaleu has been replaced on the UEFA list by 20-year-old Murad Mammadov; Biel is doubtful and Sa Pinto would not say who is available, though Goldar and Pepe are back. Referee Ishmael Barbara's low card rate is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals but no longer count Lele's ban, which Balla and Indkast both confirm; he was involved in roughly a fifth of Pafos' goals, so that alone is worth about -8% on the total. Winger Ngamaleu is also out (not in the numbers) and Midtjylland are set to rotate before Copenhagen, so I go to about 2.6, not lower, as a weakened Midtjylland defence also leaks more.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, already lifted for both sides' recent corner counts. Pafos lose two wide attackers in Lele and Ngamaleu but Midtjylland's tall side brings set pieces either way, and the two pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already low because both sides have been booked rarely lately and referee Ishmael Barbara shows 3.3 a game. Quina's red was in the Cypriot league and there is nothing heated between these clubs, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent volume. Pafos without Lele and Ngamaleu lose two of their main shooters and a rotated Midtjylland, who have put Europe second, tend to create less, so I go to about 26.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, with Pafos at 5.7 after 26 on target in their last six, a run Lele helped build. Without him and Ngamaleu, and with a changed Midtjylland side, I go to about 9.1.

401915808.overall: Brann are 7th with 7 points and unbeaten in nine games in all competitions, scoring in each, so a home win would put them close to the top eight; they won a wild 4-3 at KFUM on Sunday. Their long injury list (Tronstad, Sorensen, Kjartansson, Gudmundsson, Opsahl, Boakye) is already in the numbers. AGF are 24th on 2 points with one goal in three European games, but have won their last two league games; Yakob, Tingager, Poulsen and Serra are out (counted), and Jacob Andersen took a hard stamp on the hand against Lyngby, with no word that he will miss out. About 900 AGF fans have sold out the away end, and referee Antoniou Menelaus is already counted. News was thin: no Norwegian team-news preview turned up, so this view rests on Danish reports and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 1.8 for Brann, and already count Brann's 16 goals in six and the absences of Gudmundsson and Sorensen. AGF have scored once in Europe but have conceded in 13 straight away games, which fits the numbers' split, and nothing new is out on either side, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers expect 11.8 corners, with Brann's 40 corners in six already adding 8% and AGF's few recent corners trimming theirs. Brann attacking at home for a top-eight place fits that picture rather than adding to it, so I stay at about 11.8.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.8 cards, 2.4 of them for AGF, with their recent card rate and referee Antoniou Menelaus (4.0 in his one game on record) already counted. These clubs have never met and a full away end adds noise rather than needle, so I stay at about 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, 18.5 for Brann, already lifted 10% for Brann's recent volume and cut for AGF's. AGF's two league wins came with a near-full side and nothing new keeps anyone out, so I stay at about 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target and already lift Brann (34 on target in six) and trim AGF (8 in three). Brann's side at KFUM was close to their best available, so nothing new moves it and I stay at about 10.4.

401915506.overall: Besiktas (8th, 7 points) meet Hapoel Be'er Sheva (33rd, 1 point) in Batumi, Georgia, where UEFA moved the game for security reasons; most of the crowd should still be Besiktas fans. Besiktas come off a 4-2 win at Konyaspor and have the Galatasaray derby next; Fanatik's headlines speak of 'Europe first, then the derby', while an earlier Turkish report said Vincenzo Italiano wants to limit Vlahovic's and Trossard's minutes. Fabio Miretti (shoulder) is still listed out and Agbadou and Akdag are not available, none of them in the numbers' missing list, but none is a main attacker. Hapoel are without first-choice keeper Ofir Marciano, Lucas Ventura, Dan Biton and probably Eliel Peretz, all already counted, and Danish referee Morten Krogh's low card rate is in the numbers too. I keep only a small trim on goals and shots on target for the managed minutes of Besiktas' best finishers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 2.3 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.1%) and for Marciano missing in Hapoel's goal (+6.2%). They cannot see that Italiano may manage Vlahovic's and Trossard's minutes before the Galatasaray derby; the latest headlines say Besiktas put this game first, so I trim only slightly, to about 2.84.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. Besiktas should have most of the ball against a side near the bottom of the table, and Miretti's absence in midfield or a few changes up front do not change how often they get to the byline, so I stay at about 7.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side, and already take 12% off for referee Morten Krogh's low card rate (2.9 a game). The political background brings heavy security around the game, but with a mostly Besiktas crowd and a home side expected to dominate, nothing points clearly up or down, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas, already nudged for recent form. Besiktas have named the same eleven in their last two games, and even if Vlahovic and Trossard come off early the side should keep shooting often against a weak defence missing its first-choice keeper, so I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target, 7.7 for Besiktas, already lifted for sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and trimmed for Hapoel (-5.9%). Fewer minutes for Vlahovic and Trossard, Besiktas' best finishers, would take a little off the quality of their shots, so I go slightly lower, to about 10.2.

401915519.overall: Celta (27th, 3 points) host Bournemouth (2nd, 12 points from four wins) at Balaidos, with Claudio Giraldez under pressure after Celta scored very little lately. Celta have now left striker Borja Iglesias and defender Carl Starfelt out of the squad despite a full session on Wednesday, Hugo Gonzalez is out with a thigh strain and Miguel Roman is still out; none of them is in the numbers' missing list, though Iglesias' absence already shows in Celta's poor scoring. Bournemouth miss Alex Toth, Julian Araujo and Juanlu Sanchez (all counted); Eli Junior Kroupi is not on their Europa League list, so Evanilson should lead the line, with David Brooks back among the substitutes. Both sides play league games three days later, so some rotation is likely. German referee Harm Osmers books a little more than average, which the numbers count.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.2 for Celta and 1.8 for Bournemouth, and already trim Celta for scoring only 4 in their last 6 (-4.2%). Borja Iglesias, Celta's main striker, is now confirmed out of the squad, which takes a little more off Celta, but Starfelt's absence at the back helps Bournemouth's Evanilson-led attack, so I go only mildly lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners, split fairly evenly. Bournemouth's direct, wide play and Celta's wing-backs in Giraldez's system both produce corners, and recent corner form is already in the numbers; rotation on either side changes faces more than this, so I stay at about 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already raised 13% for referee Harm Osmers (4.5 a game) and lowered for Bournemouth's few recent bookings. Nothing in the build-up suggests a heated match between two sides that have never had a rivalry, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots and already raise Celta for shooting a lot lately (+8.3%), even if few go in. Celta without Iglesias have still been shooting often from range, and Bournemouth's front line is close to full strength, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 on target and already cut Celta's share for poor accuracy (-9.6%), which largely reflects playing without Iglesias. Bournemouth keep their side up with Evanilson available and Kroupi not registered, so I stay at about 8.7.

401915517.overall: Dinamo Zagreb (9th, 7 points) host Bayer Leverkusen (7th, 9 points) at the Maksimir, both chasing a top-eight place; Dinamo won 2-0 at Sunderland last time, Leverkusen lost 1-0 at home to Marseille. Dinamo miss Scott McKenna and Robert Mudrazija (both counted) and captain Josip Misic is expected to start, with Dion Beljo, scorer of four of their five European goals, up front. Leverkusen miss Martin Terrier and Kennet Eichhorn (counted), while Boniface and Oermann are not registered; German reports say Diaby, Tella and Kofane are back after short league appearances and Guela Doue, in the numbers' missing list, has trained all week and is available again. Both sides play league games three days later, and Ukrainian referee Mykola Balakin shows few cards, which the numbers already take off. Doue's return is a small gain the numbers don't see, too small to move any stat, so I stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.1 of them for Leverkusen. Leverkusen's attack is close to full strength again with Diaby, Tella and Kofane back, but Schick is expected to lead it as before, and Doue's return at the back is a small plus against Beljo; McKenna's absence already shows in Dinamo's record, so I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 6.4 for Leverkusen, who have won a lot of corners lately (already counted, +1.5%). Leverkusen should have most of the ball while Dinamo play direct and quick in transition, the pattern their recent games already show, so I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already take 18% off for referee Mykola Balakin, who averages 2.8 a game. The Maksimir crowd can raise the temperature in a game both sides need, but that is part of Dinamo's home record, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots and already lift Leverkusen for heavy recent shooting (+6.2%). Both sides may manage minutes with league games right after, but Leverkusen's deeper squad means changes should not cut their volume, so I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 on target and already lift Leverkusen (+6.7%) after 45 on target in their last six. With the absences on both sides already in the missing list and Misic fit for Dinamo, I stay at about 10.

401915507.overall: Marseille (31st, 3 points) host Levski Sofia (10th, 7 points) at the Velodrome and need a win to keep play-off hopes alive; OM won at Leverkusen in this competition last time but then lost 3-2 at home to promoted Le Mans from 2-0 up, and coach Genesio spoke of a fragility after conceding. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is back after illness and fit, while Emerson and Derek Cornelius remain out (both in the numbers). Levski are level on top of the Bulgarian league, but Serginho, their key midfielder, missed Wednesday's training and is out of the coach's plans, per TribunaSofia and other Bulgarian outlets, and Kirilov, Sangare, Raychev and Hristov are injured; only Kirilov is in the numbers' missing list. Montenegrin referee Nikola Dabanovic books a little more than average, which the numbers count. I keep a slight lean lower on goals and shots on target for Levski's weakened attack.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 2.4 for Marseille and 0.8 for Levski, and already lift Levski a little for Emerson's absence. Levski are confirmed without Serginho, their main creator, who is not in the missing list, which trims their small share; Hojbjerg's return steadies Marseille's midfield after the Le Mans collapse. I go mildly lower, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 7.0 for Marseille. Genesio calls Levski a possession side, but away from home they usually end up defending deep, which pushes corners Marseille's way; that and both teams' lower recent corner counts are in the numbers already, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already raised 9% for referee Nikola Dabanovic (4.6 a game), lifted for Marseille's recent bookings and lowered for Levski's. A Marseille side under pressure could get frustrated, but nothing concrete points that way, so I stay at about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, 18.7 for Marseille, already trimmed for their lower recent shot count (-6.9%). goals.text: The numbers say 1.6 goals, 0.8 each. corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, split evenly. cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards, already high: Leganés took 27 cards in their last six and Sabadell are also among the most booked (45 yellows in 15 games), and the numbers add 11-16% for each side's recent run. shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, 14.9 for Sabadell, because Leganés have let opponents shoot a lot (104 in six), which the numbers count (+7.9%). shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target, 4.3 for Leganés, whose recent accuracy (33 on target in six) the numbers boost while also taking Morata's absence off their goals. 401875004.overall: Bottom side Venezia (20th, 6 points from 12, LLLWL) host in-form Bologna (9th, 18 points, unbeaten in five) at the Penzo on Friday evening; the numbers make Bologna clear favourites. goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, 1.6 of them for Bologna. corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.8 for Bologna, already raised for Bologna's 39 corners in six and Venezia's 40 conceded. Bologna lose left-sided width without Miranda but Zortea, Orsolini and Cambiaghi still drive their wide play, and Venezia play wing-backs Hainaut and Haps in a 3-5-2, so nothing new points either way; I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already lowered because Venezia have been booked only 5 times in six games. A relegation-threatened home side against a team chasing Europe could get edgy, but no referee is named yet and this is no derby, so I stay at about 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots, 14.2 for Bologna, already lifted for Bologna's 91 shots in six. Venezia under Nicola still get shots off (75 in six) even when losing, and both teams are expected to field near-settled sides, so I stay at about 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, 4.8 for Bologna, already raised for Bologna's 33 on target in six and lowered for Venezia's low accuracy. Adorante is still out, so Venezia rely on Adams and Lauberbach up front, much as in recent games; I stay at about 8.3.

401876392.overall: Brest (6th, 18 pts) host Paris FC (2nd, 23 pts) on Friday night in a top-six meeting after both won last weekend: Brest won 1-0 at Strasbourg for a third straight league win and clean sheet, and Paris FC beat Angers 4-0. The fresh previews (23-24 Nov) add nothing big beyond Doumbia's doubt, which points slightly the other way from Paris FC's thinner defence, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 1.4 for Brest and 1.5 for Paris FC, and they already count Brest's three clean sheets, Paris FC's 13 goals in six and Lala's absence. Brest have created plenty this season but missed many big chances, and Doumbia's doubtful ankle could blunt them, while Paris FC may be short in defence (Sangui counted, Camara from one site only); those pull against each other, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Brest have won only 13 corners in their last six while Paris FC have won 31, and the numbers already move both sides for that form. Both teams are expected to line up as usual (Brest have named the same XI four games running), so nothing changes how either side attacks and I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, down from about 4 because Ruddy Buquet (3.2 cards a game, below the 3.9 average) is the referee, and they already count Paris FC's 15 cards in their last six. There is no rivalry here and no discipline news, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.0 shots. Brest have been winning without creating much lately, while Paris FC have been shooting more than usual, and both trends are in the numbers' momentum. Doumbia's doubtful ankle could make Brest a little blunter, but he may still play, so I stay at 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Paris FC have hit the target 35 times in six games and Brest have allowed only 17 in their last six, with goalkeeper Selvik on three straight clean sheets, and the numbers already balance those runs. With nothing big missing that they don't know about, I stay at 8.

401879225.overall: Nottingham Forest (17th, 9 pts, two wins in 11) host Chelsea (8th, 16 pts) on Friday night, and previews from 25 November say both Oliver Glasner and Xabi Alonso are under pressure after defeats last weekend: Forest lost 2-0 at Bournemouth, and Chelsea lost 4-1 at home to Leeds and were booed off. Neco Williams (ankle) and Xaver Schlager (hamstring) are doubts. Chelsea are without Reece James, Maxence Lacroix, Jorrel Hato and Joao Pedro, whose goals the numbers already take off (-18.4%). Jamie Gittens is back in training but unlikely to play, and Moisés Caicedo, who went off after about 20 minutes against Leeds with a back problem, is the main doubt, with Josh Acheampong and Aaron Anselmino the likely centre-backs. Andy Madley referees (3.7 cards a game, already counted), and neither side has a midweek game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 1.5 for Forest and 1.1 for Chelsea, and already take Joao Pedro's share off Chelsea (-18.4%). New absences pull both ways. Forest lose Igor Jesus up front, and they have failed to score in three of their last five. But they also lose Savona at the back, Williams is a doubt, and Chelsea's makeshift centre-back pair has let in 20 goals in 11 games. With the two pulling against each other, I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 4.9 each. They already add a little for Forest's recent corner count and take 5% off Chelsea's quieter run. Without Reece James and the injured Gittens, Chelsea have less width and crossing, but both have been out for weeks, so that is in their recent figures. Glasner's 3-4-2-1 is unchanged, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. They already take 7.6% off for Andy Madley, who shows 3.7 a game, and allow for Chelsea's quieter recent run. Two managers under pressure in a game Forest need for their relegation fight point up. Caicedo, Chelsea's busiest fouler in midfield, may miss it with his back problem, which points down. These cancel out, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots and expect Forest to shoot more (14.7). After 99 Forest shots in their last six games, the numbers already add 13%. If Caicedo is out, Chelsea's midfield gets thinner and Forest could see more of the ball, but that is still not confirmed. Morgan Gibbs-White, second in the league for big chances created, is fit. I stay at 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Forest shoot often but land few (one on target from 17 at Bournemouth), while Chelsea hit the target fairly often, and the numbers weigh both. Without Igor Jesus, Forest lean even more on Liam Delap, who scored twice against Manchester City. Joao Pedro's absence is already in Chelsea's figures, so I stay at 8.6.

401882791.overall: Levante (15th, 12 pts, one point above the drop and four league games without a win) host Racing Santander (7th, 17 pts, three wins in their last four) on Friday night; the numbers make it a clear home win with about 3.8 goals. Luis Castro's side drew 1-1 with Elche on Monday thanks to a late Requena equaliser, so they get only four days' rest, which the numbers don't count. Levante's full-backs are the worry: Manu Sanchez is out for the season with a knee ligament injury and Toljan came off injured against Elche, and previews say 16-year-old Marc Santos could start at left-back; the numbers list no Levante absentees, so neither is counted. Jose Alberto's Racing beat Real Sociedad 3-2 with an unchanged side that made no changes until the 70th minute, so some rotation is possible; Mantilla, Gueye and Andres Martin are out and already counted. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, 2.6 of them for Levante, which is a lot for a side that has scored 17 in 13 games and one in their last match. I stay a little lower, about 3.6: Levante's blunt attack and short rest after Monday's game point down, while their makeshift full-backs (Manu Sanchez and Toljan out, not in the numbers) could let Racing score a bit more, which keeps the lean small. Racing's own absences (Mantilla, Gueye, Andres Martin) are already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, 7.0 for Levante. Racing concede plenty of corners (40 in their last six), which the numbers already count, and Levante attack down the wings with Brugue and Ivan Romero; with a teenage full-back, Levante may push less down the left, but that is a guess. Nothing clear either way, so I stay at about 11.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already a little lower for both sides' recent bookings. Levante are fighting to stay up and the game matters to them, but Racing are comfortable mid-table and no referee is named yet. Nothing the numbers can't see, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.6 shots, already lifted for Racing's busy recent games (+11.2% on their side). Levante's short rest and stand-in full-backs could take a little off their shooting, but Racing let opponents shoot freely (110 shots conceded in six), so the two roughly cancel and I stay at about 34.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already lowered for Levante's poor recent accuracy (-4.5%) and raised for Racing's (+4.3%). I have taken Levante's blunt attack off goals and do not count it twice here, so I stay at 10.5.

401885389.overall: This Madeira derby, the first top-flight meeting in five years, sets 15th against 13th. Marítimo have 8 points from 10 games, have not won in the league since 16 August (eight without a win, the last three lost) and have a game in hand after the Estoril match was postponed for bad weather. goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already take Gasolina, Liziero and Léo Santos off Nacional's goals (about -22% between them). Marítimo's defensive doubts, Paulo Henrique and Rafael Fernandes, which the numbers don't list, point up, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners and already add a little for Marítimo's recent corner count (+2.6%) and take a little off Nacional's (-2.0%). Marítimo at home in front of a full house should push forward, but Nacional's absentees are mostly not wide players and nothing I found clearly moves corners, so I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. They already take 7.8% off because Nacional have been booked less than usual lately, and they do not treat this game as a derby. It is the Madeira derby, both clubs are near the relegation zone and Record expects about 10,000 fans, so I lean higher by 10%, to about 4.8. No referee has been named yet, so this does not rest on him.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots and already cut Nacional's side by 7.8% for their low recent shot count. Marítimo should have more of the ball at home, while Nacional under Henriques won 1-0 twice and may sit deeper; these pull in both directions. Marítimo had six days' rest after 120 minutes in the cup, which is enough, so I stay at 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target and already add 4.2% to Marítimo because Nacional have conceded plenty on target lately. Marítimo's finishing has been poor and Nacional are missing some attacking options, but the numbers' ratings and missing list already reflect both, so I stay at 9.7.

401882796.overall: Betis are 4th with 27 points and strong at La Cartuja, while Rayo are 16th with 12 points, have not won away in six and lost 0-1 at home to Valencia last weekend. corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Betis's recent rise in corners (33 in six) already added. cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, with Rayo expected to take most of them; both sides' recent card counts and the past meetings are already counted. shots.text: The numbers say 31.0 shots, pushed up by strong recent shot counts on both sides (Rayo 104 in their last six), which they already add. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, with recent accuracy and the missing Ceballos and Morante already counted. Rayo's finishing away has been weak, which the numbers already know; I stay at 9.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Málaga's low recent corner count already taken off. Athletic attack wide through Nico and Iñaki Williams and Berenguer, which keeps corners coming, and Málaga at home have to push for a first win. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, a fairly calm game by La Liga standards, with Athletic's recent cards already counted. The referee is not named yet, and neither side has a suspension issue now that Aznou is back from his ban. A bottom side desperate for a win can get tense late on, but the numbers already know Málaga's position and form, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots, with both sides' recent shot counts already added; Athletic should take most of them. Their missing strikers change who shoots more than how often, since Terzic still has the Williams brothers, Berenguer, Djaló and Sancet. I stay at 26.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, with Málaga's better recent accuracy and Athletic's slightly worse accuracy already counted. Without Guruzeta and Sannadi Athletic lack a central finisher, but they have played that way for several weeks, which their recent form already shows. I stay at 8.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, with Las Palmas' corner count trimmed by momentum and Andorra's raised a little. Andorra's switch to a back three and a high press could change the shape of the game, but nothing points clearly to more or fewer corners, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.8 cards and already add a lot for Andorra's recent run (25 cards in six games, momentum +18%), which includes the reds for Owono and Solozábal. No referee is named yet and I found nothing beyond what that form already shows, so I stay at 5.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.0 shots, with Las Palmas' own count trimmed for momentum (-8%) and Andorra's raised (+10%). Small, because Solozábal's ban is now counted.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target and already credit Andorra's recent accuracy (+8% momentum) and their backup goalkeeper situation after Owono's ban. For the same reason as the shots, Las Palmas getting Viti and Sergio Ruiz back, I nudge it to about 9.2.

401882297.overall: Albacete are 20th, one point from safety, after five straight wins ended with a 1-0 loss at Burgos (a Carlos Neva own goal). goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Albacete get Corpas back from his ban, a return the numbers have not moved for, so I nudge it to about 2.35. Tenerife's run of draws and low scoring is already counted and keeps the lean small.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners and already add for Albacete's heavy recent corner count (43 in six games, momentum +5%). Corpas' return on the wing fits that pattern rather than changing it, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.3 cards and already add a lot for both sides' recent card counts (momentum +15% and +17%). shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots, with Albacete's recent volume already counted (+4% momentum). Corpas back adds an attacking option the numbers did not have during his ban, so I nudge it to about 24.7. Tenerife's low attempt count of late (58 in six) is already in the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.1 shots on target and already trim both sides for poor recent accuracy. Albacete still miss Puertas and Obeng and Tenerife have scored little; nothing new points either way, so I stay at 7.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners and already cut Eldense's share for their very low recent count (14 in six games). Calleja wants his side to keep the ball more, but nothing concrete in the news changes the picture, so I stay at 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.8 cards and already add for Eldense's recent card count (22 in six). Both sides lose a player to a fifth yellow, which shows how often they get booked, and that is in the numbers; no referee is named yet, so I stay at 5.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.7 shots, with both sides trimmed for recent momentum. Girona's main attackers, including Vanat, are available and the doubts (Bryan Gil, Jastin) are already counted, so I stay at 23.7.
