shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target, already raised for Cambuur's sharp recent shooting (39 on target in six, +11.8%) against a Sparta side that has leaked chances. Nothing new to add, so I stay at 11.3.

401883100.overall: Fran Escribá's Real Valladolid (12th, 19 points) host Real Sociedad B (19th, 13 points, in the drop zone) at Zorrilla on Saturday night; the numbers make Valladolid favourites with about 2.5 goals. The Sanse lost 0-3 at home to Cádiz on 21 November and finished with nine men: Alex Marchal and Gorka Carrera, two of their front three, are banned (the numbers count both), and Iñaki Rupérez is also out (the RFEF list has him banned for yellow cards, FotMob lists a muscle injury), which the numbers do not count. Valladolid drew 1-1 at Celta Fortuna with a young side; striker Juanmi Latasa was held back there, Diario de Valladolid said Escribá was 'almost convinced' he would be ready for this game and a COPE headline on 24 November says the club 'recovers' him (I could not open the article), while the numbers still take him out (FotMob lists him until early December), so I add a little to Valladolid's goals. Trilli is out for about a month and Guille Bueno is only easing back after a long injury. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, 1.5 for Valladolid, after taking 7.6% off their goals for Latasa and 6.8% off the Sanse's for Carrera's ban. Diario de Valladolid said Latasa would be ready and a COPE headline says he is back, so that deduction looks too large; he may start on the bench after injury, so I give back only part of it, +4%, about 2.6. The Sanse's other absences (Marchal, Rupérez) and their 0-3 home defeat do not suggest they will score more.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 6.0 for Valladolid, already raised for both sides' busy recent corner counts (40 for Valladolid in six). Escribá calls his side offensive and the Sanse play out from the back as a reserve side does; nothing on lineups or tactics points either way, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already high for Segunda and raised a little for the Sanse's recent bookings, including the two second-yellow red cards against Cádiz and Rupérez's fifth yellow. A relegation-threatened young side away from home can pick up cards, but the numbers already see their record, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at about 6.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, already lifted for the Sanse's busy recent shooting against Valladolid's open defence (+13.9%). Without Marchal and Carrera the Sanse front line is weaker, but the numbers count both bans, and Latasa's return changes who shoots more than how often; I stay at about 29.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target, already raised for Valladolid's sharp recent shooting (40 on target in six, +8.0%). With Latasa, their first-choice striker, reported fit after being left out at Celta Fortuna, I add a little, +3%, about 9.5.

401885385.overall: Two struggling sides meet in Guimarães on Saturday night. Tiago Margarido's Vitória (14th, 9 points) were knocked out of the Taça de Portugal 0-2 at home by Braga on 21 November, after which he criticised his side's attitude and aggression in the first half, and a defeat here could drop them toward the relegation places. Pepa's Estrela (12th, 10 points) have lost five league games in a row, the last 2-3 at home to Benfica, but stopped the slide in the cup with a 1-0 home win over Portimonense on 22 November. Vitória are without Castillo, Francisco Dias and Gui and Estrela without Jeremy Arévalo (back injury since the start of the season); the numbers already count all of them. No referee is named yet, and I found nothing beyond this that the numbers miss, so I stay with them on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 for Vitória. Estrela have leaked goals during their five league defeats (13 conceded in six) and the numbers already add for that and for Vitória's absentees, while Vitória's own attack looked blunt against Braga. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 5.9 for Vitória. As the home side needing a win Vitória should push forward, and Margarido said his full-backs struggled to find space against Braga; both sides' recent corner counts are close to normal and already in the numbers, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. Vitória are under pressure after the cup exit and their coach asked for more aggression, while Estrela have been booked less than usual lately, which the numbers already take off; with no referee named yet I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, 14.9 for Vitória. Vitória had only one shot in the first half against Braga but pressed hard after the break, and Estrela have been shooting more than expected lately, which the numbers already count. I stay at about 24.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target, 4.8 for Vitória. Estrela's accuracy has dropped during their losing run and the numbers already trim them for it; neither side has a new absence up front, so I stay at about 7.6.

401875538.overall: A relegation six-pointer: ADO Den Haag are 17th with 9 points and FC Utrecht 15th with 12 after 13 games, and Utrecht have conceded 37 goals, the second most in the league. Both clubs have changed coach this month: ADO sacked Robin Peter on 2 November and Maurice Steijn lost 3-0 at Ajax on his return last Sunday after Matteo Waem was sent off; Utrecht sacked Anthony Correia on 22 November after a 2-3 home loss to promoted Cambuur, and Jong Utrecht coach Mark Otten takes his first game as interim. Waem's ban is already in the numbers; ADO otherwise report almost a full squad (only striker Luka Reischl, who has not scored this season, is out with a groin injury), while Utrecht winger Angel Alarcon missed the Cambuur game with a slight injury and full-back Niklas Vesterlund pulled out at the last minute, both unclear for Sunday. Utrecht's director said stability and the goals conceded are the first job for Otten, and with so much at stake for both I lean a little lower on goals and a little higher on cards. News was thin four days out: no preview for this match was published yet, so the view rests on match reports, club news and the coaching changes.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, high because both defences leak (ADO 28 conceded, Utrecht 37), and they already add about +6% for Utrecht because ADO defender Waem is banned. I lean slightly lower: Utrecht's interim coach Mark Otten has been told stability and cutting the goals conceded come first, and a bottom-four meeting with two new coaches often starts cautious. That takes it to about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, with Utrecht taking a bit more (5.0) and recent form already counted (ADO slightly below expected for, Utrecht slightly above). Neither coaching change points clearly to more or less wide play yet: Steijn's only game was played with ten men at Ajax, and Otten has no Eredivisie match behind him. I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, with Utrecht's busier recent card count (+3%) already in; no referee is named yet and the brief flags no stakes. This is a tense relegation six-pointer between two sides under new coaches, and ADO picked up a red card and a late heavy challenge (Sylla on Mokio) at Ajax, so I lean mildly higher, to about 3.7. If the referee is named, his record will be counted by the numbers, not by me.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, and they already add about +15% to Utrecht for their recent shot volume against a side that has allowed many shots. Against Cambuur Utrecht had one shot on target before half-time and then pushed hard, which fits that count; Otten's focus on defending could trim it, but that is only a hunch, so I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target (4.9 ADO, 5.8 Utrecht), with recent form already counted on both sides. ADO managed only four shots at Ajax, but with ten men for most of the game, so that says little about Sunday; Utrecht's striker Artem Stepanov scored against Cambuur and Alarcon's fitness is unclear. Nothing the numbers can't see points either way, so I stay at about 10.7.

401875031.overall: A bottom-of-the-table meeting: Udinese are 19th with 6 points and still without a home win, Fiorentina 16th with 9 after a 3-0 defeat at Monza, so both badly need the points. Udinese's new coach Paolo Zanetti (Runjaic has left) got his first point in a 1-1 draw at Bologna, but striker Keinan Davis is doubtful again with an adductor relapse, Bertola and Idrissa Gueye are out and Ebosse is racing to be fit; Karlstrom is one booking from a ban. Fiorentina coach Vanoli has sent the squad into a training camp from Thursday and Florence reports say this game is decisive for his job, with a switch back to a more cautious 4-3-3 expected. Fiorentina's defence is short: Pongracic and Parisi are out and Viery is in serious doubt after going off injured at Monza, leaving Ranieri and Dragusin in the middle. None of these absences are in the numbers' missing list; they already count only recent form (more shots, fewer cards) and the head-to-head, and no referee was named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already lifted a little for Fiorentina's recent scoring, Udinese leaking goals and past meetings. Both defences are among the three worst in Serie A and Fiorentina are missing Pongracic and probably Viery, which the numbers don't know, but Udinese may lose Davis, their main striker, with Bayo or Zaniolo up front instead. With a nervous relegation game and Vanoli expected to go back to a safer 4-3-3, I lean mildly lower, to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.3 corners and already add a little for both teams winning more corners than usual lately. Fiorentina's change from 4-2-3-1 to 4-3-3 with Njie wide and Udinese's wing-backs like Abankwah both keep play going down the flanks, and nothing I read points clearly either way, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards, already pulled down because both sides, Udinese especially, have picked up fewer cards than expected in their last six games. This is a tense six-pointer at the bottom with Fiorentina's coach reportedly playing for his job and the squad in a training camp, which tends to bring more fouls and protests, and Karlstrom and Dragusin are both one booking from a ban. The referee is not yet named; I lean a little higher, to about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.8 shots and already push them up strongly for recent form: Udinese and especially Fiorentina have been shooting more than expected, and both have allowed plenty. Davis being doubtful takes away Udinese's main target, while Fiorentina's weakened back line should let Udinese shoot more; these roughly balance, so I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target, already raised a lot for recent form (Fiorentina +15%, Udinese +7%). Without Davis, Udinese's striker, their attempts are more likely to be from distance and off target, and Fiorentina's more cautious set-up could mean fewer clear chances, so I lean slightly lower, to about 9.6.

401879229.overall: Everton (9th, 16 pts) host Liverpool (4th, 21 pts) in the Merseyside derby on Sunday lunchtime. Everton come in off a 4-0 defeat at Brentford on Monday in which captain James Tarkowski was sent off; he starts a three-match ban, Michael Keane or Jake O'Brien are expected to partner Jarrad Branthwaite, and Jack Grealish is back in David Moyes' squad after a disciplinary absence. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 but play away at Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday night, leaving under four days before kick-off; Cody Gakpo (calf, confirmed out for the derby by Iraola) and Ryan Gravenberch (heel/fascia, no return date) both missed the United win and are not in the numbers' missing list. The numbers already count Tarkowski's absence, Liverpool's strong recent attacking form and the derby's extra cards; no referee is named yet, so I only trim Liverpool's attacking output a little for Gakpo and the short turnaround.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals (Everton 1.1, Liverpool 1.6), already including Tarkowski's ban (about -8% on Everton, +6% on Liverpool) and Liverpool's 15 goals in their last six. Gakpo is out and the numbers don't know it, and Liverpool play in Bruges on Wednesday before a Sunday lunchtime derby; they did score four against United without Gakpo or Gravenberch, so I only trim it slightly, to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with Liverpool's 53 corners in their last six already pushing their side up by about 10%. Gakpo's absence takes away one wide outlet, but Liverpool have Ngumoha, Munoz and Barcola for the flanks and Everton have just been pinned back in a 4-0 loss, so nothing new points either way; I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, and that already includes the derby boost (about +39%), which is the main reason it is above a normal Premier League game. No referee has been named yet, and Everton's captain Tarkowski, sent off for a high tackle on Monday, is banned, which removes one aggressive defender rather than adding anything; with no new information the numbers can't see, I stay at 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.2 shots, with Liverpool at 18.1 after a +19% boost from their 122 shots in the last six games. That form was partly built with Gakpo, who now misses the derby, and the Champions League trip to Bruges on Wednesday plus a 12:00 kick-off may blunt their tempo; I trim a little to about 29.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target (Everton 4.2, Liverpool 5.0), already counting both sides' recent form. Gakpo's absence and Liverpool's short turnaround after Brugge are the only new factors, and Liverpool's forwards (Isak, Wirtz, Ngumoha, Munoz) are still strong, so the trim is small: about 8.9.

401882787.overall: Valencia are 17th with 12 points but come off a 1-0 win at Rayo; Osasuna are 13th with 15 points after beating Málaga at El Sadar. Osasuna, under Jagoba Arrasate, lose centre-back Catena to suspension (Herrando is expected to replace him) and miss goalkeeper Aitor Fernández, Bretones and Yeboah; the numbers already count Catena and Bretones. Aimar Oroz is back from injury and only had his load reduced this week, and Rosier missed a session for personal reasons but is expected to be available. Javier Aguirre's Valencia are without Jesús Vázquez and Diego López (counted), while Danjuma is a doubt after being given leave following his father's death; Otorbi is available again. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, with Valencia expected to score most of them; they already take about 8% off Osasuna for Catena's ban and add about 6% each to Valencia for Catena and Bretones missing at the back. Danjuma's doubt for personal reasons could cost Valencia a forward, but Raba or Otorbi can cover, and Oroz's return helps Osasuna create. Those roughly balance, so I stay at 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, with Valencia's low recent corner count (20 in six) and the many corners they conceded (42) already counted. Aguirre's side play direct to Sadiq more than they build down the wings, and Osasuna under Arrasate are a solid mid-block team. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, already higher on Osasuna's side for their recent card count (19 in six, Catena's red among them). No referee has been named, so his record can't be judged yet. A relegation-zone home side against a physical Osasuna can get scrappy, but the numbers already know both sides' form, so I stay at 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots, with Valencia's low recent shot count (55 in six) and Osasuna's good output against Valencia's leaky defence already counted. Oroz returning gives Osasuna more creativity, while Danjuma's doubt could take a little off Valencia. Nothing clear moves it, so I stay at 24.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.2 shots on target, a low figure that already reflects Valencia's poor recent accuracy (17 on target in six) and the past meetings. With Sadiq or Hugo Duro up front for Valencia and Oroz back to supply Osasuna's forwards, I see no reason to move it. I stay at 7.2.

401882794.overall: Barcelona lead with 36 points from 13 games (12 wins) and visit 12th-placed Deportivo, who have 15 points and are led in attack by Aubameyang (five goals). Barcelona play Sabah in Baku on Wednesday and host Atlético on 2 December, so some rotation is possible. Fermín López's two-match ban was confirmed on 25 November after the appeal failed (the numbers count it), but Lamine Yamal, whom the numbers count as out, stayed home from Baku only as a precaution with mild ankle discomfort and the club says he is expected to be available at Riazor. Joan García (knee) and Christensen are doubts or out, and Rodri may only get minutes off the bench. Deportivo, under Antonio Hidalgo, get striker Eddahchouri back after wrist surgery but are still without defender Bright Ede; no referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, but they take about 17% off Barcelona's scoring for Lamine Yamal being out, and the club now says his ankle problem is minor and he is expected to play at Riazor; Fermín's ban, also counted, is confirmed, so that part stands. I size it at +8%, to about 3.3, rather than adding back the whole amount, because Yamal's fitness is still the club's expectation and he could be managed with Atlético coming on Wednesday. Deportivo missing defender Ede, which the numbers don't know, also leans slightly towards more goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, with Barcelona's lower recent corner count (28 in six) already taken off. Barcelona should have most of the ball and Yamal on the right usually drives play wide, but the numbers' corner figures for Barcelona are not reduced for his absence, so his return adds nothing here. I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, already raised for Deportivo's recent card count and the many cards Barcelona have drawn lately. The referee has not been named, and Fermín's red against Villarreal is behind his ban, which doesn't change how many cards this game should bring. I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, with Barcelona expected to take about 19 and their recent high shot count (114 in six) already added. The numbers' shot figures don't take anything off for Yamal, so his expected return doesn't add to them, and possible rotation before Atlético pulls slightly the other way. I stay at 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy already counted. Eddahchouri back for Deportivo gives them another option up front with Aubameyang, but that changes who shoots more than how often. I stay at 10.4.

401883103.overall: Granada are 4th, unbeaten in almost two months under Pacheta, though an eight-game winning run ended with a 1-1 at Sabadell. Ceuta are bottom with 5 points and five straight defeats, the latest a 2-3 home loss to leaders Almería on Monday in which Cedric Teguia scored and was then sent off; his ban is in the numbers. Ceuta changed coach on 12 November: Sergio Lobera wants possession and attacking football, and their recent games under him (lots of shots and corners) are already in the numbers. Granada's top scorer Alejandro Marqués trained apart on Wednesday with minor discomfort after Sabadell, defender Pau Casadesús is out and Owen is away at the U17 World Cup; Diallo, Sergio López and Alcaraz are managing loads but should be available. Granada then go to Almería in the Copa on Wednesday 2 December, part of a heavy December; no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already add for Ceuta's leaky run (15 conceded in six) and take a little off for Teguia's ban. I lean slightly lower, to about 2.8: Marqués, Granada's top scorer, trained apart with discomfort after Sabadell and the numbers do not list him; it is only a doubt four days out, so the size stays small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and already move a lot for recent form: Granada's very low count (13 in six, -6%) and Ceuta's high one under Lobera (51 in six, +13%). Nothing in the news changes how either side wins corners, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.7 cards and already add for Ceuta's recent bookings (+11% momentum), including Teguia's red against Almería. No referee is named yet and I found nothing the numbers can't see, so I stay at 5.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots and already lift Ceuta's attempts a lot for their recent volume (111 in six, +24%), which fits Lobera's attacking style. Marqués' doubt matters more for finishing than for how often Granada shoot, so I stay at 26.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target and already credit both sides' recent accuracy (+6% and +11% momentum). Without a fully fit Marqués, Granada's most dangerous finisher, I nudge it down slightly to about 9.2.

401882295.overall: Mallorca are 6th and unbeaten in seven, but four of their last five were draws, the latest 0-0 at Tenerife, and local press notes some unease around coach Luis García. Castellón top the table after beating Eldense 2-0 and have conceded only five goals all season; midfielder Pablo Santiago says they come to play on equal terms with a squad that is all available, apart from long-term absentee Fabrizio Brignani (knee, counted). Mallorca still miss Antonio Sánchez, Jan Salas, Morlanes, Dani Luna and Antoniu Roca, with John Donald and left-back Alberto Moreno doubts, while centre-back David López has recovered, earlier than the numbers' list says. None of these absences moved the numbers much, and Castellón face five games in 15 days. No referee is named yet; nothing points clearly away from the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already rate Castellón's defence (five conceded in 15 games) and Mallorca's recent scoring. David López back early helps Mallorca's back line a little and Alberto Moreno is a doubt, which roughly cancel out, so I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Castellón's Pablo Santiago singled out Mallorca's set pieces as a threat, but that is how Mallorca usually play and it is in their record already, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.9 cards and already add for Mallorca's games drawing cards lately (+8% momentum) and Castellón's (+5%). A top-six meeting with Mallorca needing a win could get tense, but no referee is named and nothing new points either way, so I stay at 5.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.0 shots, with both sides trimmed a little for momentum. Castellón say they will not defend passively and Mallorca need to win at home, but both fit what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 23.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target and already include Mallorca's good recent accuracy and Castellón's tight defence. Mallorca's missing midfielders (Morlanes, Antonio Sánchez) were not moving the numbers and nothing new points either way, so I stay at 8.0.

401875535.overall: Feyenoord (5th, 25 points) host leaders-chasing Ajax (2nd, 28 points) in De Klassieker on Sunday. Feyenoord under Giovanni van Bronckhorst have gone seven games without a win, lost the last four including 2-3 at home to Excelsior and 0-1 to Porto in the Champions League on Tuesday, when Kastenmeier debuted in goal; defenders St. Juste, Bos and Beelen are listed out, with Moder doubtful, and the numbers have no team news for this match. Ajax under Míchel are unbeaten for over a month, with Brandt, Berghuis, Kehrer and Gaaei back, but Dolberg, Adingra, Tsygankov and Mokio are out; they host Thun in the Conference League on Thursday and are expected to rest Brandt and Gaaei there with Sunday in mind. Allard Lindhout referees (his second Feyenoord-Ajax); the numbers already add about 39% to cards for the derby.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take a little off Feyenoord (7 goals in their last six) and add to Ajax (16). Feyenoord's back line is without St. Juste, Bos and Beelen, which helps Ajax, but Ajax are without their striker Dolberg (Marcos Leonardo leads the line) and these absences have lasted weeks, so they are largely in the recent form already; recent Klassiekers were tight (1-1, 2-0, 2-1, 0-2), so I stay at about 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with Feyenoord taking most of them at home (6.5). A Feyenoord side desperate to end its losing run should push forward, and Ajax concede plenty of corners lately (35 in six), but the numbers already count both, so I stay at about 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add about 39% for the derby. Allard Lindhout was named on 23 November and the numbers assume an average referee; I found no card record for him that points either way, so I stay at about 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.4 shots and already nudge Ajax up for recent form. Feyenoord played a full Champions League game on Tuesday while Ajax plan to rest key players against Thun on Thursday, which slightly favours Ajax's freshness, but Feyenoord at home should still have the larger share of shots; nothing clearly moves the total, so I stay at about 28.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10 shots on target and already take 7% off Feyenoord for their lack of finishing lately and add 5% to Ajax. Feyenoord again lacked the final pass against Porto by VI's account, which the form figures already reflect, so I stay at about 10.

401875534.overall: Fortuna Sittard (7th, 23 points) host Heerenveen (6th, 24 points), two in-form sides chasing the European play-off places: Heerenveen under Robin Veldman have won five in a row, the last 2-1 at Groningen with two goals from Dylan Vente, and Fortuna are unbeaten in five after winning 1-0 at Go Ahead Eagles on 22 November. Fortuna had a turbulent week, with coach Danny Buijs announcing he will leave at the end of the season and commotion over the club's annual accounts. Fortuna are without wingers Zeefuik and Romeny, midfielder Michut, defender Sinkgraven and first-choice keeper Branderhorst (Koopmans deputises), with Oukili doubtful; the numbers carry no Fortuna team news. Heerenveen miss Petrov, which the numbers count. Jannick van der Laan referees, as the numbers assume; news for this match was thin, with no dedicated preview found.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and count Heerenveen's 16 goals in six and Petrov's absence. Fortuna are without two first-choice wingers (Zeefuik, Romeny) and Michut, none of whom the numbers list, and lean on Descotte and Ihattaren for goals; their recent form shows part of this, so I lean mildly lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners and already take 5% off Fortuna for few corners lately (18 in six) and note they concede many (47). Losing their wide players is part of why Fortuna win fewer corners, which the form figure already shows, so I stay at about 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.9 cards and already add a little for Jannick van der Laan (3.2 per game). Both sides have been booked slightly less than usual lately, which is counted, and Buijs's announced departure does not point to a more heated game, so I stay at about 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots and already take 5% off Fortuna for their low shot count lately (59 in six). With Zeefuik, Romeny and Michut still out and Oukili doubtful, Fortuna's attack stays thin beyond what the form average catches, so I lean mildly lower, to about 25.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target and already take 8% off Fortuna and add 5% to Heerenveen for recent form. The same missing Fortuna attackers point slightly lower, so I move it to about 9.4.

401875532.overall: PEC Zwolle (11th, 15 points) host AZ (4th, 26 points) on Sunday evening. PEC have a new coach, Alex Pastoor, appointed during the international break after Henry van der Vegt left; he won his debut 3-1 at Telstar, extending an unbeaten run of five, and PEC are without Krastev, Rahajaän and Van der Wal. AZ under Lee-Roy Echteld beat Sparta Rotterdam 5-1 last weekend but play Sparta Prague away in the Europa League on Thursday night, and striker Mexx Meerdink and defender Elijah Dijkstra did not travel because they were not fit; Smit, Schouten, Patati and Hornkamp are also out (the numbers count Smit, Schouten and Hornkamp, but not Meerdink or Dijkstra). Marc Nagtegaal referees, as the numbers assume.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and already take a little off AZ for Smit, Schouten and Hornkamp. Striker Meerdink was not fit to travel to Prague (NOS and NH Nieuws), which the numbers don't know, and AZ play there on Thursday night before this Sunday game; Meerdink could still recover, so I lean mildly lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners and already count PEC's 34 corners in six and AZ conceding few. Pastoor's arrival may change PEC's approach, but one game is too little to read, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards and already take about 15% off for Marc Nagtegaal, who books about 2.7 per game. Both sides' card counts lately are close to normal and nothing about the stakes points to a heated game, so I stay at about 2.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots and already add 11% to AZ for 100 shots in their last six. With Meerdink doubtful, Smit and Hornkamp out and a trip to Prague three days earlier, AZ's attack may be less sharp than that run, so I lean mildly lower, to about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target, most of them AZ's (5.9). The same doubts over Meerdink and the Thursday Europa League trip point slightly lower, so I move it to about 9.1.

401874992.overall: Bottom-three Sassuolo (18th, 8 points) host Napoli (8th, 18 points). corners.text: The numbers expect 9.5 corners, 5.6 for Palace at home, already counting Palace conceding plenty of corners lately and Hull winning more. Frank's first home game should see Palace push forward, which fits that split, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.0 cards, already raised because both sides have been booked more than usual lately, and they count Jarred Gillett's average card rate. It is a tense game for a bottom side, but nothing new points to more cards than that, so I stay at about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 26.4 shots, 16.4 of them from Palace.
